root_cause.text: The DMA dequeue abort logic in the mipi-i3c-hci driver unconditionally issues a ring abort without checking if the ring is already stopped, neglects to reinitialize the completion before each wait, and clears the RING_CTRL_ENABLE bit during abort—leading to potential hangs, incorrect wait behavior, or disruption of hardware state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch checks `ring_status & RING_STATUS_RUNNING` before issuing abort, adds `reinit_completion(&rh->op_done)`, writes `RING_CTRL_ENABLE | RING_CTRL_ABORT` to preserve enable, and treats an already stopped ring as success—directly addressing the four flaws listed in the commit message.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer` (lines 465-507) contains all three vulnerable constructs: (1) It unconditionally writes RING_CTRL_ABORT without checking RING_STATUS to see if the ring is already stopped (line 469: `rh_reg_write(RING_CONTROL, RING_CTRL_ABORT);`). (2) It calls `wait_for_completion_timeout(&rh->op_done, HZ)` without reinitializing the completion before the wait (line 470). `rh->op_done` was initialized only once in `hci_dma_init` via `init_completion`, so a previously completed completion may cause the wait to return prematurely.
